claims.text: New computational methods or interatomic potentials can design high-entropy alloys with optimized local chemical order.
Optimizing local chemical order will improve alloy strength.
Optimizing local chemical order will improve alloy ductility.
Optimizing local chemical order will improve fracture resistance.
Computationally designed high-entropy alloys with optimized local chemical order will provide an improved combination of strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
The predicted improvement will apply under varying temperatures and loading conditions relevant to structural applications.
Current state-of-the-art high-entropy alloys have limited combinations of strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
Current computational methods and potentials have limitations that constrain the proposed design approach.
Experimental challenges in synthesizing and characterizing new high-entropy alloys constrain the proposed approach.
The relationships among alloy composition, microstructure, local chemical order, and mechanical properties are uncertain.
